title: Devolution of Interest in Coparcenary Property — Section 6 HSA

content.overview: Section 6 of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956 governs devolution of a deceased Hindu’s interest in Mitakshara coparcenary property. The 2005 amendment made daughters of a Mitakshara coparcener coparceners by birth with the same rights as sons. On death, the interest devolves by testamentary or intestate succession under the Act, not by survivorship alone, subject to the statutory scheme.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Mitakshara coparcenary interest? (2) Daughter’s equal birthright post-2005? (3) Testamentary or intestate devolution? (4) Notional partition / computation?
content.study:
Section 6 is the core coparcenary-devolution provision of the HSA after the Hindu Succession (Amendment) Act, 2005.

Daughter of a Mitakshara coparcener becomes a coparcener by birth in her own right in the same manner as a son, with the same rights and liabilities.

On death of a Hindu leaving an interest in Mitakshara coparcenary property, the interest devolves by testamentary or intestate succession under the Act, and not by survivorship alone, subject to the section’s scheme including notional partition for computation where required.

Do not invent case holdings. Case-law verification (including daughter’s retrospective application questions) remains a separate evidence-backed gate.

sections.heading: Daughter as coparcener (2005)
sections.body: Daughter of a Mitakshara coparcener is a coparcener by birth with the same rights as a son.

sections.heading: Devolution not by survivorship alone
sections.body: Interest devolves by testamentary or intestate succession under the Act, subject to the section.

sections.heading: Notional partition for computation
sections.body: Where the statute requires, interest is ascertained as if a partition had taken place immediately before death.

sections.heading: Link to intestate rules
sections.body: Intestate devolution follows the Class I / other schedules under the Act once the interest is ascertained.

hypotheticals.question: Does survivorship alone dispose of Mitakshara interest after the amendment?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 6 provides for devolution by testamentary or intestate succession under the Act, not by survivorship alone.

distinctions.title: s. 6 coparcenary interest vs s. 8 separate property intestacy
distinctions.right: Separate property intestate succession for males under s. 8.

misconceptions.trap: Daughters still take only as heirs under the old limited scheme.
misconceptions.correction: Post-2005, daughters are coparceners by birth with the same rights as sons under s. 6.
